name: Hazel Fraser
life: “I still remember taking my traveling stool on my last day at work.” People around Harbour Bakery know Hazel by a small Friday habit. Hazel buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I brought my own folding stool because being offered a chair makes me feel ancient.
appearance: Hazel has a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Look for silvery hair gathered at the nape. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cropped bottle-green coat with a train token tied to a zipper pull. In conversation Hazel listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Hazel takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To sit on the familiar stool for a complete performance.
family: Cara Holt is Hazel’s cousin. Hazel checks the date twice. Cara brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The first straight paycheck*, Cara says, “I used to arrest him. We're both waiting at the same bank window and I want to let him greet me first.”
connections: Hamish Baxter. A familiar stool gives the hesitant listener a place to pause the performance.

reactions.situation: A young actor asks the listener to stop the pocket play
reactions.response: Hazel lets the actor stop without calling the audience's attention to the interruption.
reactions.asWritten: A young actor asks the listener to stop the pocket play. Hazel lets the actor stop without calling the audience's attention to the interruption.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Hazel takes it to a staffed counter with a second person present and leaves contact details for the owner.

reactions.situation: When a relative dismisses a little luxury
reactions.response: Hazel asks which ordinary pleasure the relative would give up first.
